## 5.5 Baseline-Rate Departure × Time Trend

The trend-active stress scenario activates both factors simultaneously. Here we
*cross* them in a 2×2 design (baseline-rate departure × time trend) to see how each
changes rejection probability, and whether their joint contrast differs from the
additive prediction.

This is a factor-crossing experiment, **not** mechanism isolation. Both factors feed
the monitoring rule, the SSR trigger and the RAR allocation rule simultaneously, and
the design does not separate those channels. We also describe the departures as
departures from the calibration anchor $p_0 = 0.25$, not as quantified prior–data
conflict, which would have to be defined against the prior predictive distribution.

```{r departure-trend-crossing}
#| cache: true
#| fig-cap: "Rejection probability in the baseline-rate-departure by time-trend crossing under Rule B. Trend-active cells impose contemporaneous equality between arms but use a time-constant analysis. The annotated interaction is a point estimate; its propagated 95% Monte Carlo simulation interval includes zero."

cat("Factor crossing: 2x2 baseline-rate departure x trend\n")
mech_grid <- expand.grid(
  conflict = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  trend    = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)

# Per-cell seeds, for the same reason as the factorial: the four cells differ
# in how often SSR fires, so a shared sequential stream leaves each cell at a
# different offset and contaminates the four-cell interaction contrast.
# Indexing with [[ ]] on the data frame row also avoids apply()'s coercion of
# the logical grid to character.
t1e_mech <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(mech_grid)), function(k) {
  row <- mech_grid[k, ]
  set.seed(400000L + 1000L * k)
  p_c <- if (row[["conflict"]]) p0_conflict else p0   # 0.30 vs 0.25
  d   <- if (row[["trend"]])    delta_trend  else 0    # 0.05 vs 0
  # H0: p_true_e = p_c_data (both arms at same rate, MAP prior is what conflicts)
  t1e_at(replicate(N_sim_sens,
    simulate_one_trial(mix    = prior_mix,
                       p_true_e = p_c,   # H0 preserved: same rate as control
                       p_c_data = p_c,
                       delta    = d,
                       use_ssr  = TRUE,
                       use_rar  = TRUE)), gamma_star)
}, numeric(1))

mech_res <- mech_grid |>
  mutate(T1E   = t1e_mech,
         label = case_when(
           !conflict & !trend ~ "Anchor, no trend\n(independent run)",
           conflict  & !trend ~ "Departure only\n(no trend)",
           !conflict & trend  ~ "Trend only\n(at anchor)",
           conflict  & trend  ~ "Both\n(trend stress)"
         ))

# Additive prediction vs. actual
t1e_neither  <- mech_res$T1E[!mech_res$conflict & !mech_res$trend]
t1e_conf_only<- mech_res$T1E[ mech_res$conflict & !mech_res$trend]
t1e_trend_only<-mech_res$T1E[!mech_res$conflict &  mech_res$trend]
t1e_both_mech<- mech_res$T1E[ mech_res$conflict &  mech_res$trend]

additive_pred <- t1e_conf_only + t1e_trend_only - t1e_neither
interaction_term <- t1e_both_mech - additive_pred

cat(sprintf("Departure only:   %.4f  (+%.4f vs. anchor run)\n",
            t1e_conf_only,  t1e_conf_only  - t1e_neither))
cat(sprintf("Trend only:       %.4f  (+%.4f vs. anchor run)\n",
            t1e_trend_only, t1e_trend_only - t1e_neither))
cat(sprintf("Additive prediction: %.4f\n", additive_pred))
cat(sprintf("Observed (both):     %.4f\n", t1e_both_mech))
cat(sprintf("Interaction term:    %+.4f  (point estimate; MC uncertainty below)\n",
            interaction_term))

mech_res |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(label, T1E,
             fill = factor(conflict + trend * 2,
                           labels = c("Neither","Departure","Trend","Both")))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.52) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed",
             color = ZET$red, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = additive_pred, linetype = "dotted",
             color = ZET$slate, linewidth = 1.0) +
  # ── in-panel annotation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # This figure carries no title or subtitle: the manuscript prints a caption
  # beneath every figure, so a title only repeats it. What the subtitle used to
  # carry is annotated inside the panel instead.
  #
  # The three positions below were checked against the bar tops, their value
  # labels and the legend box at the rendered 9 x 5.5 in size; each has under
  # one line height of slack in at least one direction. Re-check before nudging.
  #
  # Additive-prediction label: left-hand end, sitting just above the dotted line
  # it names rather than floating mid-gap, so the label and its line read as one
  # object. Offset is in data units off additive_pred, not a fixed y.
  annotate("text", x = 0.55, y = additive_pred + 0.0035,
           label = sprintf("Additive prediction: %.4f", additive_pred),
           size = 4.1, fontface = "bold", color = ZET$ink, hjust = 0) +
  # The arc runs from the additive-prediction label to the observed value on the
  # "Both" bar. Its two endpoints are the two numbers whose difference IS the
  # interaction, so the span carries the meaning and the label above it only has
  # to name the quantity. Both endpoints sit above every bar, so the path stays
  # clear however the bar heights move; offsets are taken off the data rather
  # than hardcoded for the same reason.
  # Both endpoints are referenced to additive_pred rather than to one endpoint
  # each. The two quantities differ by the interaction, which is ~0.0006 here, so
  # anchoring the arc to t1e_both_mech at one end made it visually level anyway
  # while leaving it free to collide with the dotted line if the gap ever widens.
  # Riding above additive_pred keeps a fixed clearance over the line, the "Both"
  # bar and that bar's value label at the same time.
  # The arc runs number to number: it starts just right of the "0.1146" inside
  # the additive-prediction label and ends just left of the "0.1140" above the
  # Both bar. Those two numbers are what the interaction is the difference of,
  # and they happen to sit at almost the same height (0.1181 vs 0.1180), so the
  # span reads as a comparison rather than as a rise. The endpoints track the
  # label heights, not the bar tops, so they stay attached if the values move.
  annotate("curve", x = 1.80, y = additive_pred + 0.0035,
           xend = 3.68, yend = t1e_both_mech + 0.0040,
           curvature = -0.16, angle = 90, ncp = 12,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           color = ZET$green, linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.74, y = additive_pred + 0.0270,
           label = sprintf("Interaction point estimate = %+.4f", interaction_term),
           size = 4.1, fontface = "bold", color = ZET$green, hjust = 0.5) +
  # Short form for the nominal-alpha line: the caption spells it out in full,
  # and only the gap between the first two bars is wide enough for a label.
  # x = 1.68, not 1.5: the first bar's value label is centred at x = 1 and sits
  # at almost exactly this height, so 1.5 left the two nearly touching.
  annotate("text", x = 1.68, y = alpha, label = "α = 0.025",
           hjust = 0.5, vjust = -0.45, size = 3.5,
           fontface = "bold", color = ZET$red) +
  # Value labels clear the nominal-alpha line. A bar whose top sits within a
  # label height of alpha would otherwise have the dashed line struck through
  # its own label -- which happened to the 0.0232 and 0.0248 bars, both of which
  # land within 0.002 of 0.025. y is mapped explicitly (vjust = 0, bottom-
  # aligned) rather than nudged, so the offset is in data units and survives a
  # change of y-limit.
  geom_text(aes(y = T1E + ifelse(abs(T1E - alpha) < 0.006, 0.0080, 0.0020),
                label = sprintf("%.4f", T1E)),
            vjust = 0, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold", color = ZET$ink) +
  # No key. The fill maps to the same four categories the x axis already names,
  # in the same order, so it encodes nothing position does not -- the legend
  # entries were just abbreviated tick labels. The fills stay: they separate the
  # reference condition from the composed one at a glance. Contrast Figure 2,
  # where two series share one pair of axes and colour is the only thing telling
  # them apart; that legend is load-bearing and stays.
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Neither  = ZET$neutralF,
                                Departure = "#2563EB",
                                Trend    = ZET$teal,
                                Both     = ZET$green),
                    guide = "none") +
  # 1.20 was sized for the older, lower arc. The arc now rides above the dotted
  # additive line and the interaction label sits above the arc, so the label
  # needs about 1.27; 1.30 leaves it roughly a line of headroom without opening
  # a band of empty panel above it. Checked in the matplotlib preview.
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(t1e_mech) * 1.34),
                     labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Rejection probability", fill = NULL) +
  theme_zetyra() +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", color = ZET$ink,
                                  margin = margin(t = 4, r = 4)),
        axis.text  = element_text(size = 13, color = ZET$slate))
```

```{r departure-trend-table}
tribble(
  ~Condition, ~`Rejection probability`, ~`vs. anchor run`, ~Note,
  "Anchor, no trend (independent run)", t1e_neither, "—", "independent reference cell",
  "Departure only (no trend)", t1e_conf_only,
    sprintf("%+.4f", t1e_conf_only - t1e_neither),  "baseline away from calibration anchor",
  "Trend only (at anchor)", t1e_trend_only,
    sprintf("%+.4f", t1e_trend_only - t1e_neither), "rate drifts from anchor",
  "Both (trend stress)",      t1e_both_mech,
    sprintf("%+.4f", t1e_both_mech - t1e_neither),  sprintf("interaction = %+.4f", interaction_term)
) |>
  mutate(`Rejection probability` =
           sprintf("%.4f", `Rejection probability`)) |>
  kable(caption = paste("2x2 crossing of baseline-rate departure and time trend.",
                        "Both factors feed the full pipeline, so this",
                        "crosses factors rather than isolating mechanisms."),
        align = c("l","r","r","l"))
```

## 5.6 Rejection Probability Across the Common-Rate Grid

For superiority, $H_0:p_e\le p_c$; the common-rate family $p_e=p_c=p$ is its
equality boundary. The first sweep sets $\delta=0$ and estimates pointwise Type
I error along that boundary. A violation at any evaluated point is enough to
disprove uniform control, but this sweep neither establishes the least-favorable
configuration nor evaluates the interior $p_e<p_c$. A second, explicitly
separate sweep retains the shared
calendar trend used in the trend-active stress scenario. In that DGM,
$p_e(i)=p_c(i)$ for every enrollment index $i$, but the arms need not sample
the same calendar periods. With RAR disabled, the implemented rule
`arm = (i - 1) %% 2` gives deterministic strict alternation: control occupies
odd enrollment positions and experimental treatment occupies even positions.
By construction, this balances arm counts at even looks and tightly interleaves
enrollment time, but it is not exact time balance under the coded patient-level
trend. At every
even look, experimental patients are systematically one position later within
each pair, so their average generating rate exceeds control by
$\delta/(N_{\mathrm{base}}-1)=0.05/89\approx0.00056$; at the odd $n=45$ look,
the arm counts differ by one. With RAR active, allocation additionally depends
on accumulating data. The analysis remains time-constant in both cases. We
therefore report these values as rejection probabilities under contemporaneous
no treatment effect and analysis-model misspecification, not as Type I error
for the paper's constant marginal-rate null.

Both sweeps hold $\gamma^*$ at the value calibrated for the full design at
$p=0.25$ and $\delta=0$. The comparison series merely disables SSR and RAR; it
is a fixed-threshold ablation, not a separately calibrated monitoring-only
design.

Three caveats govern how the sweeps should be read.

**Finite-grid contrasts are not sharply identified.** Each row is a Monte Carlo
estimate and the grid is discrete. Locating a crossing in a fixed-$\gamma^*$
contrast would require a denser grid and preferably paired common-random-number
contrasts; the tables support statements only about the evaluated points.

**The SSR rule shares a threshold with the sweeps.** SSR is a pooled blinded
nuisance-parameter rule under a working 1:1 Wald calculation, while the
operational allocation is response-adaptive and the final estimand is the
Bayesian two-arm comparison $p_e>p_c$. Any contrast involving SSR therefore
belongs to this prespecified working rule and should not be generalized to all
blinded SSR procedures.

**Extended trials accrue more drift in the stress sweep.** With drift anchored
to the planned horizon $n_{\text{base}}=90$, Rule B's largest attainable final
sample size of $n=100$ experiences terminal drift
$0.05\times99/89\approx0.0556$, rather than $0.05$ at the planned terminal
position. A longer trial therefore spans more calendar time. This is part of
the stated trend-active DGM, but it is absent from the constant-rate
equality-boundary sweep.

```{r composite-null-sweep}
#| cache: true

# Each series uses disjoint per-cell seeds. The trend-active seed blocks preserve
# the prior analysis; the static-null blocks are new and non-overlapping.
run_null_sweep <- function(delta, seed_disabled, seed_full) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(p_null_grid), function(i) {
    pn <- p_null_grid[i]
    set.seed(seed_disabled + 1000L * i)
    disabled <- t1e_at(replicate(
      N_sim_sens,
      simulate_one_trial(
        mix = prior_mix, p_true_e = pn, p_c_data = pn, delta = delta,
        use_ssr = FALSE, use_rar = FALSE)), gamma_star)

    set.seed(seed_full + 1000L * i)
    full <- t1e_at(replicate(
      N_sim_sens,
      simulate_one_trial(
        mix = prior_mix, p_true_e = pn, p_c_data = pn, delta = delta,
        use_ssr = TRUE, use_rar = TRUE)), gamma_star)

    tibble(
      p = pn,
      `SSR + RAR disabled` = disabled,
      `All mechanisms` = full,
      `Fixed-gamma* difference` = full - disabled,
      `MCSE (ablation)` = mcse(disabled, N_sim_sens),
      `MCSE (full)` = mcse(full, N_sim_sens),
      `MCSE (difference)` = sqrt(
        mcse(disabled, N_sim_sens)^2 + mcse(full, N_sim_sens)^2))
  }))
}

composite_null_static <- run_null_sweep(
  delta = 0, seed_disabled = 900000L, seed_full = 1000000L)
contemporaneous_null_trend <- run_null_sweep(
  delta = delta_trend, seed_disabled = 600000L, seed_full = 700000L)

format_null_sweep <- function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(
      across(
        c(`SSR + RAR disabled`, `All mechanisms`,
          `MCSE (ablation)`, `MCSE (full)`, `MCSE (difference)`),
        ~ sprintf("%.4f", .x)),
      `Fixed-gamma* difference` =
        sprintf("%+.4f", `Fixed-gamma* difference`))
}

format_null_sweep(composite_null_static) |>
  kable(caption = paste(
    "Pointwise Type I error along the constant-rate equality boundary",
    "(p_e = p_c = p, delta = 0). Both series hold the full-design threshold",
    "gamma* fixed; 'SSR + RAR disabled' is an ablation, not a separately",
    "calibrated design. Monte Carlo standard errors are conditional on gamma*."),
    align = rep("r", 7))

format_null_sweep(contemporaneous_null_trend) |>
  kable(caption = paste(
    "Rejection probability under contemporaneous no treatment effect",
    "(p_e(i) = p_c(i), delta = 0.05) with a time-constant analysis.",
    "Both series hold the full-design threshold gamma* fixed. Read the",
    "difference against its own MCSE; individual rows near zero are not",
    "distinguishable from no difference at N = 5,000 per cell."),
    align = rep("r", 7))
```

```{r composite-null-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=5.2, fig.cap="Pointwise rejection probability across the common-rate grid under Rule B. The left panel is the constant-rate equality boundary of the superiority null and reports Type I error; the right panel is a shared-trend contemporaneous no-effect stress scenario analyzed with a time-constant model. Grey holds the full-design threshold gamma* with SSR and RAR disabled; green is the full design. Both are fixed-threshold comparisons, not separately calibrated designs. Dashed red line = nominal alpha = 0.025."}
null_plot_data <- bind_rows(

null_plot_data |>
  select(p, DGM, `SSR + RAR disabled`, `All mechanisms`) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`SSR + RAR disabled`, `All mechanisms`),
               names_to = "Design", values_to = "Rejection") |>
  ggplot(aes(p, Rejection, color = Design, shape = Design)) +

    `SSR + RAR disabled` = ZET$neutralL,

  theme(axis.title  = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold", color = ZET$ink,

## 5.7 Sensitivity Analysis


All three sweeps pass the relevant parameter directly into `simulate_one_trial()`.
No global variables are mutated. These are **frozen-threshold perturbations**:
each setting retains the anchor-calibrated $\gamma^*$, rather than being
recalibrated as a new design. The 95% simulation intervals show Monte Carlo
uncertainty conditional on that threshold.

```{r sens-prior-weight}
#| cache: true
# Swept quantity is the weight on the FLAT robustify() component: larger
# w_vague = less borrowing from the historical prior.
w_grid <- seq(0, 0.90, by = 0.10)
set.seed(300L)

t1e_w <- sapply(w_grid, function(w) {
  t1e_at(replicate(N_sim_sens,
                 simulate_one_trial(mix    = set_vague_weight(prior_mix, w),
                                    p_true_e = p0_conflict,
                                    p_c_data = p0_conflict,
                                    delta    = delta_trend,
                                    use_ssr  = TRUE,
                                    use_rar  = TRUE)), gamma_star)
})

sens_w <- tibble(
  w = w_grid,
  t1e = t1e_w,
  se = mcse(t1e_w, N_sim_sens),
  lo = pmax(0, t1e - 1.96 * se),
  hi = pmin(1, t1e + 1.96 * se))

p_w <- sens_w |>
  ggplot(aes(w, t1e)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              fill = ZET$green, alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(color = ZET$green, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = ZET$green, size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed", color = ZET$red) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Vague-Component Weight", x = bquote(w[vague]),
       y = "Rejection probability") +
  theme_zetyra()
```

```{r sens-time-trend}
#| cache: true
delta_grid <- seq(0, 0.15, by = 0.025)
set.seed(400L)

t1e_d <- sapply(delta_grid, function(d) {
  t1e_at(replicate(N_sim_sens,
                 simulate_one_trial(mix    = prior_mix,
                                    p_true_e = p0_conflict,
                                    p_c_data = p0_conflict,
                                    delta    = d,          # varied here
                                    use_ssr  = TRUE,
                                    use_rar  = TRUE)), gamma_star)
})

sens_d <- tibble(
  d = delta_grid,
  t1e = t1e_d,
  se = mcse(t1e_d, N_sim_sens),
  lo = pmax(0, t1e - 1.96 * se),
  hi = pmin(1, t1e + 1.96 * se))

p_d <- sens_d |>
  ggplot(aes(d, t1e)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              fill = ZET$green, alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(color = ZET$green, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = ZET$green, size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed", color = ZET$red) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Time Trend Magnitude", x = bquote(δ),
       y = "Rejection probability") +
  theme_zetyra()
```

```{r sens-ssr-timing}
#| cache: true
ssr_grid <- c(20L, 30L, 40L, 45L, 55L, 60L)
set.seed(500L)

t1e_ssr <- sapply(ssr_grid, function(nt) {
  t1e_at(replicate(N_sim_sens,
                 simulate_one_trial(mix      = prior_mix,
                                    p_true_e   = p0_conflict,  # H0: p_e = p_c = p0_conflict
                                    p_c_data   = p0_conflict,
                                    delta      = delta_trend,
                                    n_ssr_trig = nt,       # varied here
                                    use_ssr    = TRUE,
                                    use_rar    = TRUE)), gamma_star)
})

p_ssr <- tibble(
  nt    = ssr_grid,
  t1e   = t1e_ssr,
  se    = mcse(t1e_ssr, N_sim_sens),
  lo    = pmax(0, t1e - 1.96 * se),
  hi    = pmin(1, t1e + 1.96 * se),
  label = sprintf("n=%d\n(%d%%)", ssr_grid,
                  as.integer(round(ssr_grid / N_base * 100)))
) |>
  ggplot(aes(label, t1e)) +
  geom_col(fill = ZET$green, width = 0.55, alpha = 0.90) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.14,
                linewidth = 0.6, color = ZET$ink) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed", color = ZET$red) +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = sprintf("%.4f", t1e)),
            vjust = -0.25, size = 3.5, color = ZET$ink) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(pmin(1, t1e_ssr +
                                             1.96 * mcse(t1e_ssr, N_sim_sens))) * 1.18),
                     labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "SSR Trigger Timing", x = bquote(n[SSR]),
       y = "Rejection probability") +
  theme_zetyra()
```

```{r sens-panel, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Frozen-threshold sensitivity of rejection probability to prior weight (left), time trend (centre), and Rule B timing (right). Bands and bars are pointwise 95% Monte Carlo simulation intervals conditional on gamma*. Dashed line = nominal alpha = 0.025."}
p_w | p_d | p_ssr
```

  ~Parameter, ~Range, ~`Observed rejection range`, ~`Largest MCSE`,
  "Vague-component weight (w<sub>vague</sub>)", "0% – 90%",
    sprintf("%.4f – %.4f", min(t1e_w), max(t1e_w)),

## 5.8 Reproducibility

**Append-only grid extension, and what it demonstrated.** The common-rate grid
was extended from seven points to nine (adding $p = 0.40$ and $0.45$) after the
seven-point results had been reviewed. Both sweeps seed per grid *position*
(`seed_base + 1000*i`), so appending the new rates left $i = 1,\dots,7$
untouched, and the seven original rows were expected to reproduce exactly.

The development comparison found all 42 retained point estimates across both
sweeps — ablation, full design, and their difference at seven rates in two
sweeps — bit-identical before and after the extension; the MCSEs are
deterministic functions of the corresponding proportions. The pre-extension
render was overwritten and is not part of the release, so this comparison is
recorded rather than independently auditable from the released files. The
per-cell seeding nevertheless ensures that appended points cannot perturb the
random streams used by earlier positions.

Had a point been *inserted* rather than appended, every position after it would
have shifted, silently reseeding every subsequent cell and changing numbers
that had already been reviewed. Any future extension of this grid should
likewise append.

```{r auto-summary}
#| code-fold: false
cat(sprintf("gamma*                = %.3f\n", gamma_star))
cat(sprintf("Type I error (calibration)  = %.4f  (target: %.3f)\n",
            t1e_at_star, alpha))
cat(sprintf("Type I error (fresh anchor) = %.4f  (95%% SI [%.4f, %.4f])\n",
            anchor_validation_t1e,
            anchor_validation_ci["lower"], anchor_validation_ci["upper"]))
cat(sprintf("Rejection probability (+2 pp from anchor, p=0.27) = %.4f  (+%.1f%%)\n",
            t1e_mild, inflation_pct_mild))
cat(sprintf("Rejection probability (+5 pp from anchor, p=0.30) = %.4f  (+%.1f%%)\n",
            t1e_primary, inflation_pct))
cat(sprintf("Rejection probability (earlier SSR, n_ssr=30) = %.4f  (+%.1f%%)\n",
            t1e_neg, (t1e_neg - alpha)/alpha*100))
cat(sprintf("Max constant-rate null Type I error on grid = %.4f\n",
            max(composite_null_static$`All mechanisms`)))
cat(sprintf("Max trend-active rejection probability on grid = %.4f\n",
            max(contemporaneous_null_trend$`All mechanisms`)))
cat(sprintf("Earlier-vs-reference change = %+.4f (%+.1f%% of stress excess)\n",
            timing_change, timing_change_pct_excess))
cat(sprintf("\nFixed-threshold factorial ablation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Delta_SSR         = %+.4f\n", delta_f_ssr))
cat(sprintf("  Delta_RAR         = %+.4f\n", delta_f_rar))

cat(sprintf("  Trend only        = +%.4f\n", t1e_trend_only - t1e_neither))

```{r mcse-table}
mcse_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Estimate,                     ~Probability,   ~N_sim,
  "Calibration (in-sample at gamma*)", t1e_at_star, N_sim_calib,
  "Independent anchor validation", anchor_validation_t1e, N_sim_sens,
  "+2 pp from anchor + trend (p=0.27)", t1e_mild, N_sim_main,
  "+5 pp from anchor + trend (p=0.30)", t1e_primary, N_sim_main,
  "Trend stress: earlier SSR (n = 30)", t1e_neg, N_sim_main,
  "Factorial: baseline",         t1e_f_base,     N_sim_sens,
  "Factorial: SSR only",         t1e_f_ssr,      N_sim_sens,
  "Factorial: RAR only",         t1e_f_rar,      N_sim_sens,
  "Factorial: SSR + RAR",        t1e_f_both,     N_sim_sens,
  "Departure x trend: neither",  t1e_neither,    N_sim_sens,
  "Departure x trend: departure only", t1e_conf_only, N_sim_sens,
  "Departure x trend: trend only", t1e_trend_only, N_sim_sens,
  "Departure x trend: both",     t1e_both_mech,  N_sim_sens
) |>
  mutate(
    MCSE   = mcse(Probability, N_sim),
    CI_lo  = Probability - 1.96 * MCSE,
    CI_hi  = Probability + 1.96 * MCSE,
    Probability = sprintf("%.4f", Probability),
    MCSE   = sprintf("%.4f", MCSE),
    `95% SI` = sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]", CI_lo, CI_hi),
    N_sim  = formatC(N_sim, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  # The calibration row is in-sample: gamma* was chosen by bisection ON this
  # same vector to be the smallest threshold achieving <= alpha, so the value is
  # near-deterministic by construction (its across-seed SD is O(1/N_sim), not
  # the binomial sqrt(p(1-p)/N_sim)). Printing a binomial MCSE and a simulation
  # interval for it would describe an estimator that was not used. The honest
  # out-of-sample companion is the row directly below it.
  mutate(MCSE     = if_else(grepl("^Calibration", Estimate), "---", MCSE),
         `95% SI` = if_else(grepl("^Calibration", Estimate), "---", `95% SI`)) |>
  select(Estimate, Probability, MCSE, `95% SI`, N_sim)

kable(mcse_tbl,
      caption = paste("Monte Carlo standard errors and 95% simulation intervals",
                      "for key rejection-probability estimates, conditional on",
                      "the selected gamma*. No-trend rows estimate Type I error;",
                      "trend-active rows are contemporaneous no-effect stress",
                      "scenarios under a time-constant analysis. The calibration row is",
                      "in-sample and near-deterministic by construction, so no",
                      "MCSE is reported for it; use the independent anchor",
                      "validation row for the out-of-sample anchor value."),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c", "r"))

# ── Propagated MCSEs for derived interaction terms ──────────────────────────
# Interaction = T1E_both - T1E_A - T1E_B + T1E_neither
# All four simulations are independent, so Var(interaction) = sum of variances

# Departure x trend interaction
se_mech <- sqrt(
  mcse(t1e_both_mech,  N_sim_sens)^2 +
  mcse(t1e_conf_only,  N_sim_sens)^2 +
  mcse(t1e_trend_only, N_sim_sens)^2 +
  mcse(t1e_neither,    N_sim_sens)^2
)

int_tbl <- tribble(
  ~`Interaction term`,                    ~Estimate,        ~MCSE,    ~`95% SI`,
  "Departure × trend", interaction_term, se_mech,
    sprintf("[%+.4f, %+.4f]", interaction_term - 1.96*se_mech, interaction_term + 1.96*se_mech),
  "Factorial (SSR × RAR; pooled)", pooled, se_p,
    sprintf("[%+.4f, %+.4f]", pooled - 1.96*se_p, pooled + 1.96*se_p)
) |>
  mutate(Estimate = sprintf("%+.4f", Estimate),
         MCSE    = sprintf("%.4f", MCSE))

kable(int_tbl,
      caption = paste("Propagated MCSEs for derived interaction terms.",
                      "The factorial row is the inverse-variance pooled estimate",
                      "from the N = 5,000 and N = 20,000 per-cell runs reported above.",
                      "Intervals are Monte Carlo simulation intervals, not",
                      "sampling-confidence intervals for clinical data."),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c"))
```

**Seeds:**

| Simulation | Seed |
|---|---|
| MAP prior MCMC | 42 (via `set.seed()` before `gMAP()`) |
| RAR validation | 42 |
| Threshold calibration | 1 |
| Calibration-threshold bootstrap | 2 |
| Independent anchor validation | 101 |
| Trend stress: +5 pp from anchor (p=0.30) | 2026 |
| Trend stress: +2 pp from anchor (p=0.27) | 2028 |
| Earlier-SSR timing sensitivity (n<sub>SSR</sub> = 30) | 2027 |
| Fixed-threshold factorial ablation | per cell: 300000 + 1000·k, k = 1..4 |
| Departure × trend (2x2) | per cell: 400000 + 1000·k, k = 1..4 |
| Fresh-seed interaction check | per cell: 800000 + 1000·k, k = 1..4 |
| Shared-trend grid — ablation series | per grid point: 600000 + 1000·i, i = 1..9 |
| Shared-trend grid — full design | per grid point: 700000 + 1000·i, i = 1..9 |
| Constant-rate null grid — ablation series | per grid point: 900000 + 1000·i, i = 1..9 |
| Constant-rate null grid — full design | per grid point: 1000000 + 1000·i, i = 1..9 |
| Sensitivity — prior weight | 300 |
| Sensitivity — time trend | 400 |
| Sensitivity — SSR timing | 500 |

#| code-fold: false
# Also written to disk. Printing into the rendered HTML records the producing

```{r map-prior-release-restate}
#| cache: false
# Restates the preflight outcome beside sessionInfo() so the release record
# carries it, and re-reads the committed file to confirm the object that
# actually fed the simulations is still that file. That last identity IS a hard
# stop wherever it runs: if it fails, the results in this document were not
# produced by the committed prior, which is a correctness failure rather than
# an environment difference.
map_release_check <- unname(dget(MAP_FROZEN_PATH))
dimnames(map_release_check) <- list(c("w", "a", "b"), NULL)
stopifnot(identical(prior_mix, map_release_check))
cat(sprintf("Simulation input: %s (confirmed unchanged)\n", MAP_FROZEN_PATH))
cat("Layer 1, published 4 dp prior table: PASS (hard gate)\n")
cat(sprintf("Layer 2, refit reproduces the frozen mixture: %s  (max dev %.3e, bound %.0e)\n",
            if (map_frozen_ok) "yes" else "NO -- see the preflight warning",
            map_frozen_dev, MAP_FROZEN_TOL))
cat(sprintf("Release-certifiable render: %s\n",
            if (map_frozen_ok) "yes" else
              "NO -- reproduction is valid, certification is not"))
cat("Status written to map_prior_status.txt; asserted by ",
    "tools/release/check_release.py --only map_prior\n", sep = "")
